findings.title: Blocklist lookup is case-sensitive, so mixed-case addresses bypass it
findings.description: `should_block?` runs `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` on the raw address. The signup path never normalizes the address. `User.new_from_params` (app/models/user.rb:84-91, called from users_controller.rb:160) assigns `params[:email]` as typed, and `User` has no before-validation normalization. PostgreSQL `=` is case-sensitive, so a blocked `bad@spamclub.com` can be registered as `Bad@SpamClub.com`. `Email.downcase` (lib/email.rb:19-22) is not sufficient on its own, because it lowercases only the domain. Normalize both the stored entry and the lookup (for example, full `downcase`), and add a spec with mixed-case input. The `change_email` path (users_controller.rb:269) already uses `Email.downcase`, so the two entry points are inconsistent.

findings.title: Validator mutates match counters, so each attempt is counted twice
findings.description: `EmailValidator` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?` (app/models/blocked_email.rb:11-18), which increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, and saves. Validation should be side-effect free. In `UsersController#create`, `user.valid?` runs at users_controller.rb:168 and `user.save` runs at line 172, which validates again. Each blocked attempt therefore inflates `match_count` by 2. The read-modify-write (`match_count += 1; record.save`) also loses increments under concurrent requests, and a failed `save` is ignored silently. Keep `should_block?` a pure predicate, record the match in one place, and use an atomic counter update such as `BlockedEmail.update_counters`.

findings.title: Domain restriction regex has no end anchor, so suffix domains pass the whitelist
findings.description: `Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true)` is unanchored at the end. With a whitelist of `vaynermedia.com`, `someone@vaynermedia.com.attacker.example` matches and is accepted. Registration requires confirming the address from the inbox, which the attacker controls on that domain. This logic is copied unchanged from `User#email_in_restriction_setting?`, so the flaw predates this diff. The diff moves it into a new file, and the existing whitelist specs (spec/models/user_spec.rb:535-552) do not cover the suffix case. I reasoned about this from the regex semantics and did not run it. The fix is to anchor with `\z` and escape each domain with `Regexp.escape`. The current `gsub('.', '\.')` leaves other metacharacters unescaped.

findings.title: New blocklist and rejection behavior has no end-to-end or controller tests
findings.description: Both examples stub `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, so no test runs a real blocked row through `User#valid?`. The case-bypass and double-count issues above would pass this suite. In spec/controllers/users_controller_spec.rb:471-481, the `failed signup` examples assert only `success`, so the new `errors` and `values` keys are untested. No JavaScript test under `test/` references `createAccount` or `rejectedEmails`. Add a User-level spec with a real `BlockedEmail` row and mixed-case variants, a controller spec for the response shape, and a JS test for the rejection flow.

findings.title: `rejectedEmails` is one array shared across all controller instances
findings.description: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` sits in the `extend()` literal, so every instance of the class shares one array. `pushObject` at line 275 mutates that shared array. The app uses the controller as a singleton, so the impact is latent today. Any second instance, such as a test that creates a fresh controller, inherits earlier rejections. Initialize the array in `init` with `this._super()` and `this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A([]))`.

findings.title: Rejection UX is misleading and sticky
findings.description: A rejected address always shows the generic "invalid" reason, even when the server said "not allowed" or "already taken". Rejections also persist until the page reloads, so an address rejected for a reason that later changes stays blocked in this session. Consider showing the server's message on the field and clearing the list on modal open.

findings.title: `should_block?` returns `nil` rather than `false` when there is no record
findings.description: The spec says "returns false" (spec/models/blocked_email_spec.rb:22-24) but uses `be_false`, which also accepts `nil` in RSpec 2.13, so the spec does not check the contract. Use `record.present? && ...` to return a real boolean.

findings.title: Minor style issues in the new validator file
findings.description: Line 13 uses `and` where `&&` is the usual form in this codebase. The file has no trailing newline (line 24).

findings.title: Moving the domain restriction into a validator preserves behavior
findings.description: `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?` keeps the same gating as the old `validate :email_validator, if: :email_changed?`. `lib/validators` is on the autoload path (config/application.rb:36). No code calls the removed `User#email_validator` or `email_in_restriction_setting?`. The existing blacklist and whitelist specs in spec/models/user_spec.rb:488-565 still exercise the logic through `User` validation.

findings.title: Migration and locale keys are consistent
findings.description: The timestamp is later than the newest existing migration (20130723212758). The repo has no `db/schema.rb` or `db/structure.sql`, so there is no schema file to keep in sync. The unique index matches the model's uniqueness validation. The `user.email.blocked` and `user.email.not_allowed` keys exist in config/locales/server.en.yml:733-734.
